CP-6 (Alternate Storage Site) ensures equivalent controls are in place at the alternate site for stored backup information, enabling preservation and thus verifiability of restoration assets.

CP-2 (Contingency Plan) explicitly identifies essential mission and business functions and associated contingency requirements, which inform post-incident operational norms for critical mission functions.

PM-1 (Information Security Program Plan) provides an organization-wide overview of requirements for the security program and common controls, enabling consideration of cybersecurity risk management after incidents.

RA-9 (Criticality Analysis) identifies critical system components and functions through a criticality analysis, directly supporting the identification of critical mission functions to be restored post-incident.

CP-9 conducts backups of user-level information, system-level information, and documentation, providing the foundational data needed to restore systems and services following an incident.

SI-7 employs integrity verification tools to detect unauthorized changes to software, firmware, and information, which directly supports verifying the integrity of assets that have been restored following an incident.

AU-11 retains audit records for a defined period, supporting preservation of collected incident data and metadata over time.
AU-12 provides audit record generation for relevant event types, contributing systematic collection of system data that supports incident data and metadata gathering.

SI-7 uses integrity verification tools to detect unauthorized changes to information, directly supporting preservation of integrity for collected incident data and metadata.

SI-5 requires dissemination of security alerts, advisories, and directives to identified personnel and external partners, supporting the sharing of incident information across boundaries.
